claim: The Città Alta funicolare is operated by ATB, climbs 85 m over 240 m of track (max 52% gradient) and terminates at Piazza Mercato delle Scarpe, with weekday ascending service from 07:00 to 20:20 (school period), to 01:15 on Saturdays and 07:40–midnight on Sundays/holidays.
quote: Weekdays (school periods, ascending): 7:00 am to 8:20 pm ... Saturdays & weekdays (non-school periods, ascending): 7:00 am to 1:15 am ... Sundays/holidays (ascending): 7:40 AM to midnight ... terminating at Piazza Mercato delle Scarpe with a vertical rise of 85 meters over 240 meters of track at a maximum 52% gradient.

claim: Cappella Colleoni opens March–October 09:30–12:30 and 14:00–18:30, closed Mondays, free admission; it houses Bartolomeo Colleoni's equestrian monument and the tomb of his daughter Medea.
quote: March – October: 9:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. and 2 p.m.-6:30 p.m. ... Closed Mondays ... Free admission ... equestrian monument dedicated to the military commander Bartolomeo Colleoni ... tomb of Medea, his daughter

claim: Bergamo's Venetian Walls were inscribed by UNESCO in 2017 as part of the transnational 'Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th Centuries' serial site; built in 1561, they run ~6 km around the Upper Town with 14 bastions and four monumental gates (San Giacomo, Sant'Agostino, San Lorenzo, Sant'Alessandro).
quote: official designation in 2017 as part of the transnational serial site titled 'Venetian defense works between the 16th and 17th centuries.' ... approximately 6 kilometers in length ... Constructed in 1561 by the Republic of Venice ... 14 bastions, 2 platforms, 4 monumental gates (St. James, St. Augustine, St. Lawrence, and St. Alexander)

claim: Piazza Vecchia centres on the Palazzo della Ragione (late-1100s, Lombardy's oldest municipal seat), the Contarini fountain with sphinx spouts (1780), the Campanone bell tower (which still chimes 100 strokes around 10 p.m.), and the Palazzo Nuovo / Angelo Mai library — a square Le Corbusier called 'an untouchable place, a perfect work of art.'
quote: the oldest existing municipal seat in Lombardy ... visitors present around 10 p.m. will hear 'as many as 100' chimes ... Gifted to the city in 1780, this elegant centerpiece features sphinx-shaped water spouts ... Le Corbusier called 'an untouchable place, a perfect work of art.'

claim: Current Città Alta hours: Campanone Tue–Fri 10:00–18:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–19:00 (€9/€6); Santa Maria Maggiore Mon–Sat 09:00–18:00, Sun split hours (€5/€2); Rocca & 19th-century museum Tue–Sun 11:00–18:00 (€5, park free 08:00–21:00); Civic Museums €3 combined.
quote: CAMPANONE (Civic Tower) & Palazzo del Podestà - Tuesday to Friday 10 am – 6 pm | Saturday – Sunday 10 am – 7 pm — €9 full, €6 reduced ... BASILICA DI SANTA MARIA MAGGIORE - Monday to Saturday 9:00 am – 6 pm | Sunday 9:00 am – 10.30am | 1:30pm – 6 pm — €5 full, €2 for visitors over 70 ... ROCCA ... €5 museum entry ... CIVIC MUSEUMS ... €3 combined ticket

claim: ATB runs the Città Alta funicular every 7–10 minutes from roughly 07:00 to 00:30; a single ATB ticket covers the ride and is interchangeable with city buses.
quote: The Funicolare di Città Alta runs every 7–10 minutes from 07:00 to 00:30 daily. It usually runs until 12:30 AM on weekdays, and weekend and holiday hours may extend slightly.

claim: For a half-day Città Alta visit by car the best play is to park in the Città Bassa (Parcheggio Città Alta on Viale Vittorio Emanuele II, or the Piazza della Libertà / San Marco garages) and walk a few minutes to the funicolare's lower station; driving into the walled town is restricted and parking inside is scarce and pricey.
quote: The Parcheggio Città Alta, located in Viale Vittorio Emanuele II, is just steps away from the lower station of the funicolare ... San Marco parking lot in Viale Vittorio Emanuele or at the adjacent Piazza della Libertà parking, from where you can choose to climb on foot along the magnificent Venetian walls, take the funicolare, or take bus number 1

claim: Brusaporto lies about 9 km southeast of Bergamo, making Città Alta a sub-20-minute drive from Da Vittorio.
quote: Brusaporto is located about 9 kilometres (6 mi) southeast of Bergamo

claim: Bergamo Jazz Summer 2026 stages two open-air evenings at the Lazzaretto — Thu 2 July and Sat 18 July (Dee Dee Bridgewater with an all-female quartet) at 21:30 — handy add-ons for a late-spring/summer weekend.
quote: Bergamo Jazz Summer is scheduled at the Lazzaretto on Thursday, July 2, 2026 at 9:30 PM and Saturday, July 18, 2026 at 9:30 PM. On July 18, Dee Dee Bridgewater will perform

claim: Through 3 May 2026 the Palazzo della Ragione hosts the free GAMeC video installation 'I tarocchi di De André', open Thursday–Sunday 11:00–19:00.
quote: the Palazzo della Ragione is free to visit and currently features a video installation called 'I tarocchi di De André' from February 20th to May 3rd, 2026, open Thursday to Sunday from 11 am to 7 pm

claim: Walking the 6 km Venetian Walls circuit is the signature panoramic experience — San Giacomo gate and the bastion overlooks deliver views over the Città Bassa, the plain to Milan and the Orobian Pre-Alps; sunset is the standout slot.
quote: San Giacomo Gate is one of the panoramic points par excellence of Bergamo ... wonderful view of the peaks of the Orobie Alps and even up to Milan ... At sunset, walk along the perimeter of the walls to enjoy a fantastic sunset.

claim: Brusaporto to Erbusco (heart of Franciacorta DOCG) is 22.9 km / about 23 minutes by car.
quote: the road distance is 22.9 km

claim: Berlucchi (Borgonato/Corte Franca) offers I Classici at €33pp (3 wines, 1.5 h), Iconici at €44pp, Berlucchi Experience at €70pp (2 h, 3 vintage wines) and Spring Experience at €85pp; tours run Sat/Sun and weekdays by reservation, in Italian or English.
quote: Berlucchi Experience €70/person Duration 2 hours … Iconici €44/person Duration 1.5 hours … Tours are offered by prior reservation, on Saturdays and Sundays, as well as during the week

claim: Berlucchi requires obligatory online reservation with credit-card or PayPal pre-payment; tastings include local cheese and handmade grissini, English guides on request.
quote: The reservation is obligatory; you will find an updated calendar in the Tours section. You can pay with a credit card or Paypal to confirm your reservation.

claim: Ca' del Bosco (Erbusco) guided tours run €70–€100+ per person for a 1.5–2.5 h cellar walk through Arnaldo Pomodoro / contemporary-art installations and a 3-wine tasting; advance booking required.
quote: Recent visitors reported paying €70-100+ per person for guided tours with tastings. One reviewer mentioned '€100€ per person' for a vintage tour, while another paid '€70,00€' for a standard experience.

claim: Ca' del Bosco visits are by appointment only, last about 1 h 30, and access to the in-house wine shop is reserved for booked visitors.
quote: Purchases at the winery's in-house wine shop are reserved exclusively for those who have made the visit

claim: Bellavista (Erbusco) tastings start at €65pp, last ~1 h 30, run daily at 10:30 and 15:00 in English or Italian, and must be pre-booked; voucher purchase is then redeemed by arranging the date with the winery.
quote: Starting from €65.00 … Tastings with tours are available any day of the week, either in the morning at 10:30 AM or in the afternoon at 3:00 PM.

claim: Bellavista offers three tiered experiences (Visit Alma 2 wines/1 h 30, Bellavista's Harvest 3 millesimati/2 h 30, Bellavista Experience vineyards + farmhouse + cellar + 3 wines/3 h) priced €25–€70pp, by appointment only.
quote: Visits are only by appointment … Visit Alma - Tasting of 2 Franciacorta wines … Bellavista's Harvest - Tasting session of 3 Franciacorta Millesimati … Bellavista Experience … Prices vary from 25€ to 70€ per person.

claim: Mosnel (Camignone di Passirano) is one of the cheapest entry points: weekend cellar walk + tasting from €10pp, choose-your-own 2-of-5 tasting €15pp, Mosnel-Style 3-wine flight €30pp, Millesimati icons (Satèn, EBB, Parosé) €40pp; English spoken, online booking via visit.mosnel.com.
quote: Saturday and Sunday visits with a guided cellar tour (approximately 30 minutes) and Franciacorta wine tasting start from €10.00 per person … 'Mosnel Style' tasting featuring 3 Franciacorta (Brut, Pas Dosé, and Satèn Millesimato) costs €30.00 per person

claim: Barone Pizzini (Provaglio d'Iseo), Franciacorta's first organic-certified producer, charges around €20 for a 4-wine tasting flight with grissini; cellar visits descend to a barrique room 10 m underground, English on request, booking required.
quote: Recent visitors reported paying €20 for four wine tastings with breadsticks … descending to 'a room 10 m below ground level, where you find the barrique cellar' … Multiple reviews confirm English tours are available upon request

claim: Antica Fratta (Monticelli Brusati) offers three tours bookable online: Classico €35pp/2 wines/1 h 30, Selection €45pp/3 wines/2 h, and Riserva €65pp/3 wines + gourmet light lunch/2 h 30 — all available in English with free cancellation 24 h ahead.
quote: Antica Fratta Classico Price: €35.00 per person … Antica Fratta Selection Price: €45.00 per person … Antica Fratta Riserva Price: €65.00 per person Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes … 3 wines plus 'gourmet light lunch'

claim: Ricci Curbastro (Capriolo) is the budget pick: museum + cellar visit with a Franciacorta Brut DOCG glass from €11.50pp, or a 3-wine flight (Brut, vintage Satèn, vintage Extra Brut) from €25.30pp, bookable online.
quote: tasting of a glass of Franciacorta Brut DOCG accompanied with breadsticks. Starting from €11.50 per person … guided tour with tasting of 3 exceptional wines … Starting from €25.30.

claim: The Strada del Franciacorta is an ~80 km signed wine route through 19 municipalities along the foot of Lake Iseo with 122 affiliated wineries plus agriturismi, distilleries and golf clubs; five themed colour-coded itineraries (Satèn yellow, PasDosé blue, Brut green, Rosé red, Extra Brut black) can be done by car, bike or on foot.
quote: a route of about 80 kilometers, which passes through 19 municipalities of Brescia … 122 affiliated Franciacorta wineries … five main itineraries: Franciacorta Satèn (yellow route), Franciacorta PasDosé (blue route), Franciacorta Brut (green route), Franciacorta Rosé (red route), and Franciacorta Extra Brut (black route)

claim: Festival di Franciacorta 2026 is confirmed for 18–20 September 2026 in Erbusco, opening dozens of normally-private estates for guided tastings with the winemakers, vertical comparisons of Satèn/Rosé/vintage cuvées, and vineyard trekking/cycling.
quote: The Festival di Franciacorta is scheduled for September 18-20, 2026, in Erbusco, Provincia di Brescia, and the dates have been confirmed

claim: The flagship Festival del Franciacorta in Cantina runs over two weekends in mid-September each year, complemented by itinerant city tastings in Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna and elsewhere.
quote: The Festival del Franciacorta in Cantina is today an unmissable event that takes place in mid September … itinerant Franciacorta Festivals … bring the tasting tables of Franciacorta producers to different cities in Italy

claim: Decanter's Franciacorta visitor guide names Ca' del Bosco and Bellavista in Erbusco as essential first stops, with Il Mosnel (16th-century cellars, 40-ha estate, themed dinners) and organic pioneer Barone Pizzini as the other must-visits.
quote: Any winery tour should start from Ca' del Bosco … Bellavista in Erbusco is another not-to-be-missed stop. Il Mosnel, belonging to the Barzanò Barboglio family, features 16th-century cellars … Barone Pizzini in Provaglio d'Iseo was the first winery to produce DOCG Franciacorta from organic grapes

claim: Sulzano-Monte Isola ferry runs year-round with crossings of about 5 minutes and departures every 15-20 minutes; bookings for the route are only available for groups of 20+, individuals buy on site.
quote: Connections between Sulzano – Monte Isola operate all year round. Crossing time is about 5 minutes, with departures every 15–20 minutes.

claim: Sulzano and Sale Marasino are the two harbours with direct ferries to Monte Isola, each running approximately every 20 minutes; other ports (Iseo, Pisogne, Lovere, Tavernola Bergamasca, Sarnico) also serve the island.
quote: The harbours with direct ferries to Monte Isola (departing approximately every 20 minutes) are Sulzano and Sale Marasino.

claim: A round-trip Sulzano-Peschiera Maraglio ferry ticket costs about €5.70 including the €1.50 Monte Isola landing fee (2022 figure); ferries run roughly every 15 minutes between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.
quote: The round-trip ticket costs €5.70 (summer 2022 pricing), which includes a €1.50 Montisola landing fee. Indicatively there are ferries every 15 minutes between Sulzano and Peschiera.

claim: The Peschiera Maraglio to Madonna della Ceriola sanctuary trail (Path 1) is 4 km with 400 m elevation gain, takes about 80 minutes one way and is rated medium difficulty.
quote: Path 1: Peschiera Maraglio to Madonna della Ceriola Sanctuary - Duration: 80 minutes - Distance: 4 km - Elevation: +400 m - Difficulty: Medium

claim: From Peschiera Maraglio the round trip to the Madonna della Ceriola summit covers ~3.5 miles with ~1,240 ft elevation gain and takes 2.5-3 hours; the trail passes through chestnut woods and the village of Cure where two marked mule tracks lead to the sanctuary.
quote: the hike from Peschiera Maraglio is considered a hard hike that covers 3.5 miles with an elevation gain of 1,240 feet and takes about 2.5–3 hours to complete

claim: Climbing to the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Ceriola gives a 360-degree panoramic view of Lake Iseo's coasts and surrounding mountains, including the Franciacorta hills.
quote: Climbing to the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Ceriola in Monte Isola means reaching one of the most panoramic places of the whole Lake Iseo, with a 360-degree view of its coasts and the mountains that surround it

claim: Guizzetti bike rental sits at Piazzetta della Farmacia in Peschiera Maraglio, open daily 9:30 a.m.-6 p.m. from 1 March to 31 October.
quote: Piazzetta della Farmacia - Località Peschiera Maraglio, Cell: +39 3402308569. The rental will be closed from November 1st to March 1st

claim: Bertelli bike rental, Via Peschiera Maraglio 154, also operates daily 9:30 a.m.-6 p.m. from March to October, a few steps from the ferry landing.
quote: Bertelli bike rental at Via Peschiera Maraglio, 154, with phone +39 0309886103 and cell +39 3384867182. This rental is closed from November 1st to March 1st

claim: Trattoria del Sole in Sensole was founded by Albina Guizzetti in 1974 and is set in a lakeside olive grove; the menu leans on lake fish like dried sardines of Iseo, tench and lavarello.
quote: founded in 1974 by Albina Guizzetti in Sensole on Monte Isola... The menu is traditional, with many dishes based on lake fish (dried sardines of Iseo, tench, lavallo).

claim: Christo's Floating Piers (18 June-3 July 2016) used 70,000 m² of yellow fabric on 226,000 high-density polyethylene cubes to connect Sulzano with Peschiera Maraglio on Monte Isola and the islet of San Paolo.
quote: 70,000 square meters of yellow fabric, carried by a modular floating dock system of 226,000 high-density polyethylene cubes installed in 2016 at Lake Iseo... connected the village of Sulzano, on the Brescia side of the lake, to the hamlet of Peschiera Maraglio on Monte Isola and the islet of San Paolo

claim: The Italian Ministry of Culture approved €2 million to convert Cà del Dutùr (the 17th-century Palazzo Zirotti in Menzino di Monte Isola, abandoned since the 1980s) into a cultural centre with one floor dedicated to a museum of Christo's Floating Piers.
quote: the Cà del Dutùr building on Monte Isola is being transformed into a cultural and exhibition center, with one of its floors becoming a museum dedicated to The Floating Piers... 2 million euros for the project

claim: Monte Isola is car-free except for residents - only mopeds, bicycles and a few buses move between the main villages.
quote: Monte Isola is a small floating paradise where there are no cars, only mopeds, bicycles and a few buses that move between the main centers of the island.

claim: Sensole and Carzano are quieter than Peschiera Maraglio; Carzano sits on the north-eastern shore and is reached by the Sale Marasino ferry, with the village of Novale overlooking it.
quote: Sensole and Carzano are little gems not to be missed, more collected, with fewer tourists... Novale overlooks Carzano and comprises a small cluster of houses arranged to look like a long balcony

claim: The traditional dried sardine of Lake Iseo is a Slow Food presidium; after 48 hours under salt the fish dry for about a month in shaded ventilated rooms, then are pressed and covered with olive oil.
quote: After 48 hours of rest under salt, the sardines are left to dry for about a month in shaded and ventilated places, then stored in containers, pressed to drain the fat, and covered with olive oil.

claim: The top-rated trail in Parco dei Colli di Bergamo is the 4.4 mi (≈7 km) Bergamo Alta: Madonna del Bosco - San Sebastiano - San Vigilio loop with 597 ft (≈182 m) gain.
quote: Bergamo Alta: Madonna del Bosco - San Sebastiano - San Vigilio, which has a 4.7 star rating from 78 reviews. This trail is 4.4 mi long with an elevation gain of 597 ft.

claim: The Astino Valley circular route is a two-hour easy walk suitable for all ages, starting at Via Astino 33 in Bergamo and passing the S. Sepolcro church, the former Vallombrosani monastery, and a section of the Lorenzo Rota botanical garden.
quote: A two-hour walk in a stunning natural context, steeped in history... An easy walk suitable for all ages, very enjoyable in every season... the church of S. Sepolcro, the adjoining former Vallombrosani monastery wisely restored... the section of the Lorenzo Rota botanical garden where biodiversity is cultivated.

claim: The direct trail to Monte Canto Alto (1,146 m) from the Pisgiù trailhead in Sorisole is 3.1 km with 630 m gain, ~2 h to the summit, rated easy by the park.
quote: Distance: 3.1 km ... Elevation Gain: 630m ... Duration: 2 hour/s ... Difficulty: easy ... Trailhead: Ristorante Pisgiu (Sorisole) ... Destination: Vetta del Monte Canto Alto at 1,146 meters elevation

claim: The San Vigilio funicular covers 630 m with a 90 m height difference from Porta Sant'Alessandro, running every 20 minutes on the city ATB ticket.
quote: The San Vigilio funicular covers 630 meters with a 90-meter difference in height and a slope ranging from 10% to 22% ... The funicular departs from largo Porta S. Alessandro ... The service runs every 20 minutes.

claim: From the funicular's top station you can link the Astino monastery loop (11.6 km, 320 m gain, ~3h25, moderate) — a popular half-day combo with Città Alta.
quote: Astino Monastery – Streets of Bergamo's Città Alta loop ... Distance: 11.6km ... Elevation: 320m gain and loss ... Duration: 03:25 ... Difficulty: Moderate hike

claim: The Pradalunga–Prati Alti–Monte Misma route is 3.4 mi (≈5.5 km) round trip with 1,505 ft (≈459 m) gain, reaching Monte Misma at 1,161 m above the Cenate / Trescore hills.
quote: the Pradalunga - Prati Alti - Monte Misma trail is highly rated (4.3 stars from 16 reviews) and is 3.4 miles long with 1,505 feet of elevation gain. This round trip route passes through Prati Alti and reaches the top of Monte Misma at 1161m elevation.

claim: The waymarked Pope John XXIII pilgrimage trail is a 22 km circular route (11.7 km out / 10.5 km back, ~6 h, easy though long, ~1021 m cumulative gain) from Sotto il Monte to Celana Caprino, returning via Pontida Abbey.
quote: Route Length: The circular route encompasses 22 total kilometers: '11.7 km in round 10.5 in return.' Duration: Approximately 6 hours total walking time—'3 outward, three in back.' Difficulty: 'long yet easy, up and down trip' ... 'gain / loss in elevation: 1021 / -1022 m.'

claim: Lake Endine offers an easy flat loop from Ranzanico of about 5.67 km with only ~10 m gain, and a full lake circuit of 14.7 km with 70 m gain, with many lakeside paths described as dog-friendly.
quote: Length & Duration: '5.67km' and '01:26' ... 'Easy hike. Great for any fitness level. Easily-accessible paths.' ... Elevation: '10m' gain and loss ... longest featured route is the #1 option at 14.7km with moderate difficulty and 70m elevation gain ... 'Many trails around Lago di Endine are dog-friendly, especially the lakeside paths.'

claim: The Cherio-Endine cycle and walking path runs roughly 40 km total at easy grade with mixed paved and unpaved surfaces, suitable for all fitness levels.
quote: Total Length: 'approximately 40 km' ... The route features both paved cycle paths and unpaved roads ... Overall Difficulty: 'easy' with 'modest' elevation gain, making it 'suitable for everyone.'

claim: Selvino has very short family walks: Monte Poieto from Aviatico is ~45 min (1 h with kids) to a refuge, picnic area and educational farm; Santuario del Perello is ~35 min from Selvino through woods.
quote: The trail leading to the top of Monte Poieto starting from Aviatico will take you about 45 minutes (calculate 1 hour with the little ones). At the top, you will find a small Educational Farm and a Refuge ... a trail that starts directly from Selvino, near the Sports Hall and goes into the woods, with ups and downs that in about 35 minutes lead to the Sanctuary.

claim: Selvino Adventure Park offers 7 treetop trails on Monte Purito with suspended bridges, ropes and zip lines for varied skill levels — an active half-day option in the Bergamo pre-Alps.
quote: The 7 trails of the Selvino Adventure Park, which wind through the trees of Monte Purito are perfect for all kinds of 'adventurers'. These are trails that are suspended in the air among the treetops, wooden bridges, ropes and fun zip lines.

claim: Crespi d'Adda UNESCO Visitor Centre at Corso Manzoni 18, Capriate San Gervasio is open Feb-Dec Mon-Fri 8:45-13:00, Sat 8:45-17:45, Sun/holidays 8:45-18:30; January weekends 9:00-17:00.
quote: January: Saturday and Sunday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM. February–December: Monday–Friday: 8:45 AM–1:00 PM; Saturday: 8:45 AM–5:45 PM; Sunday & Holidays: 8:45 AM–6:30 PM. Winter Closure: December 22, 2025–January 5, 2026

claim: Standard Crespi d'Adda guided village tour is €8 per person, free under 6, in Italian only, lasts ~90 min on weekends from late February through November.
quote: Euro 8,00 a persona; bambini omaggio fino ai 6 anni ... TOUR DISPONIBILE DA FINE FEBBRAIO A NOVEMBRE ... Duration: 1 hour 30 minutes ... Meeting point: UNESCO Visitor Centre, Corso Manzoni 18

claim: Special complete holiday tours of Crespi d'Adda on Easter Mon, 25 Apr, 1 May, 2 Jun 2026 run ~3 hours and include the village, Bertini hydroelectric plant, multimedia museum and a VR factory experience for €19/adult.
quote: special complete tours are organized lasting about three hours that include the village, the hydroelectric plant, the multimedia museum, and an immersive virtual reality experience in the factory ... €19 per adult

claim: The motorless Traghetto di Leonardo at Imbersago is a cable-and-current catamaran ferry (records from 1454, sketched by Leonardo 1513) that crosses to Villa d'Adda carrying pedestrians, bicycles and motorcycles for €1.50 per single ticket.
quote: The ferry has ancient origins, with written records dating to 1454. Leonardo da Vinci sketched a similar vessel in 1513 ... The ferry carries pedestrians, bicycles, and motorcycles—not automobiles. Single tickets cost €1.50

claim: In 2026 the Imbersago ferry runs Sat-Sun 9:00-13:00 and 14:00-18:30, with extra weekday slots 7:00-8:00 and 17:00-18:30 from 4-31 May.
quote: As of April 4, 2026, the Traghetto di Leonardo service operates on Saturdays and Sundays from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM and from 2:00 PM to 6:30 PM ... from May 4 to May 31, 2026, the ferry also operates on weekdays (Monday to Friday) from 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM and from 5:00 PM to 6:30 PM

claim: Castello Visconteo guided tours in Trezzo sull'Adda run every Sunday and holiday from 1 March; €6 adult, €3 child, tower-only €3, English private guide €90; tour 75-90 min including tower, Longobard museum and gardens.
quote: dal 1 marzo, tutte le domeniche e giorni festivi ... Standard visit: €6 adults, €3 children ... Tower only (2:30–5:00 PM): €3 adults ... English tours: €90 with private guide ... Tours last approximately 75–90 minutes

claim: The Sentiero di Leonardo cycle-pedestrian path runs 79.2 km along the Adda banks from Lecco to Milan, mainly flat and paved, passing the Paderno iron bridge, Taccani plant, Crespi d'Adda and the Imbersago ferry; doable in one day by bike, four stages on foot.
quote: Length: 79.2 km total distance connecting Lecco to Milan ... Mainly flat or with slight height differences, for the most part paved ... Cycling: Completable in one day with return by public transport ... Walking: Divided into four stages (21.3 km, 25.8 km, 15.9 km, 16.2 km respectively)

claim: Edison's Centrale Bertini at Cornate d'Adda (Via XXV Aprile 18) opened 28 Sep 1898 as Europe's most powerful hydroelectric plant and second worldwide after Niagara; offers guided tours of preserved turbines and a museum for €3 (min 10 people).
quote: Construction began February 6, 1896 and was completed in June 1898, with operations commencing September 28, 1898 ... Europe's most powerful hydroelectric plant at the time, second globally only to Niagara Falls ... Guided tours available (minimum 10 people) ... Cost: €3 per person

claim: Parco Adda Nord is a 5,800-hectare protected riverside park ideal for walking, cycling, horseback and birdwatching, containing the Crespi d'Adda UNESCO village and the Paderno iron bridge built with Eiffel-Tower-era technique.
quote: The Adda Park is a protected natural area measuring 5800 hectares ... ideal for excursions on foot, by bike or on horseback and for birdwatching ... a UNESCO world heritage site, the Crespi d'Adda workers' village ... the San Michele Bridge in Paderno, a bridge completely made from iron

claim: Accademia Carrara's 2026 headline show TAROT: Origins, Cards, Fortunes runs February 27 to June 2, 2026, billed as the largest exhibition ever dedicated to the history of tarot.
quote: TAROT: Origins, Cards, Fortunes. February 27 – June 2, 2026. The largest and most comprehensive exhibition ever dedicated to the history of tarot.

claim: The Tarocchi show is curated by Paolo Plebani and reunites the 15th-century Mazzo Colleoni for the first time in over a century, with cards from the Morgan Library and private collections joining the Carrara's holdings.
quote: the most complete fifteenth-century deck – the legendary Mazzo Colleoni – reunited for the first time in over a century after being separated among institutions including The Morgan Library & Museum in New York

claim: Accademia Carrara ticket pricing: permanent collection €10 full / €8 reduced; combined collection + exhibitions €15 / €13; a special €20 pass covers five exhibitions plus the permanent galleries.
quote: For a visit to only the permanent collection, the full price ticket is €10, and the reduced ticket is €8... The full price ticket for visiting the permanent collection and temporary exhibitions is €15.

claim: GAMeC Bergamo is at Via San Tomaso 53, open Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri 3-7pm and Sat-Sun 10am-7pm (Tuesday closed), with €10 standard / €8 reduced admission and a €1 online advance-purchase discount.
quote: Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays: 3-7 PM / Saturday and Sunday: 10 AM – 7 PM / Tuesday closed... Standard ticket: €10.00 Discounted ticket: €8.00

claim: GAMeC's 2026 program 'Pedagogy of Hope', directed by Lorenzo Giusti, dedicates the year to pedagogy inspired by Paulo Freire, with Ana Silva's textile project Eau (Feb 26 – Sept 6, 2026) and a summer Fosbury Architecture installation at Palazzo della Ragione.
quote: GAMeC of Bergamo's 2026 program... focuses its entire year on the theme of education... The project takes the title Pedagogy of Hope and is inspired by the theoretical legacy of Brazilian pedagogue Paulo Freire

claim: Museo Donizettiano is located in the Domus Magna at Via Arena 9, open Thursday–Sunday and holidays 10:00–17:00, with admission €5 full / €3 reduced (free under 18).
quote: Thursday – Sunday & Holidays: 10-17... Full admission: €5. Reduced (ages 18-26, groups of 15+): €3. Free entry for children under 18

claim: Casa Natale di Gaetano Donizetti at Via Borgo Canale 14 is open Sundays 10:00–13:00 and 14:00–17:00, with €3 admission (€2 for groups of 15+ or guided groups); weekday visits by reservation.
quote: Gaetano Donizetti's Birthplace is open on Sundays from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM and from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM... The ticket cost is 3€ (2€ for groups of 15 people at least or groups with a certified guide)

claim: Palazzo della Ragione is Bergamo's medieval town hall on Piazza Vecchia, free to enter, hosting the video installation 'I tarocchi di De André' Thursday–Sunday 11am–7pm through May 3, 2026.
quote: Free admission. Located in Piazza Vecchia. Current exhibition 'I tarocchi di De André' runs through May 3, 2026. From Thursday to Sunday 11 am – 7 pm

claim: Palazzo della Ragione preserves 14th–15th-century frescoes detached from churches and civic buildings, including fragments of Donato Bramante's Seven Sages of Antiquity painted in 1477 from the former Palazzo del Podestà façade.
quote: fragments of the Seven Sages of Antiquity painted by Donato Bramante in 1477... a precious collection of 14th-century frescoes from the former San Francesco convent

claim: The Museo delle Storie 'All in One' ticket costs €15 and is valid 48 hours, covering seven sites: Rocca/Museo dell'800, Convento di San Francesco (Bergamo 900 + photography museum), Campanone, Palazzo del Podestà/Museo del '500, Museo Donizettiano, Torre dei Caduti, and Mura di Bergamo.
